analysis.title: Evercore Inc. (EVR): Strong advisory outlook and expense discipline drive estimate upgrades; reiterate Buy
key_insights: EVR reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $4.28 vs GSe $2.33 and Visible Alpha consensus $2.52, on revenue 32% above the Street and adjusted operating margin about 475bps above consensus. The stock rose 13% on the day.

GS attributes the move to the size of the beat, no one-time factors flagged by management, no guide-down of the 4Q26 outlook, very negative investor sentiment on EVR and peers into the print, and tight expense control.
Expenses: the comp ratio fell about 50bps QoQ to 63.0% (GSe had expected flat) and non-comp expenses fell 5% QoQ while revenue rose 18% QoQ.

Management outlook through 4Q26 and into 2027 is constructive: continued large-cap momentum with backlog replenishment, a stronger sponsor franchise (industry sponsor M&A remains tepid), elevated restructuring and liability management activity, and improving private capital advisory and debt advisory activity tied to AI infrastructure financing.
Restructuring has upside from the 2028-29 debt maturity wall as issuers refinance at higher interest rates.

Revenue of $1.2bn was 32% above consensus: advisory +38% vs consensus, ECM +20%, institutional equities 4% below. Management noted below-average 3Q revenue pull-forward from 4Q, which eases concern about weak 4Q seasonality.
Revenue growth is supported by more than 50 ramping senior managing directors and a strong recruiting pipeline. More than 40% of LTM revenue came from non-M&A businesses.
ECM: healthcare, a sector EVR is skewed toward, has been strong, but management flagged a modestly weaker start to 4Q.
GS raises 2026E/27E/28E revenue by 6%/2%/1% and operating margins by 150bps/60bps/50bps. 2026E/27E EPS rise 12%/4%.

Non-comp: EVR guided its 2026 non-comp ratio to flat to slightly better YoY (previously roughly flat) and targets slower non-comp dollar growth in coming years. GS lowers 2026E/27E/28E non-comp expenses by 4%/2%/2%.

GS rolls its Q5-Q8 P/E window forward one quarter (now 4Q27E-3Q28E) and raises the multiple 0.5x to 15.0x. The 12-month price target rises 8% to $357 from $331, versus a $259.86 price (27 Oct close), implying 37.4% upside. Rating reiterated Buy.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $4.28 and better expense control drive 2026E/27E EPS up 12%/4%. The P/E multiple rises to 15.0x on a rolled-forward window, lifting the target from $331.

sector_views.rationale: GS cites high CEO confidence, financing availability, industry disruptions and strategic impetus as supports for the M&A cycle, with large-cap momentum and elevated restructuring activity.

earnings_insights: EVR 3Q26 adjusted EPS reported $4.28 vs GSe $2.33 and Visible Alpha consensus $2.52, reported 10/28/2026 (report dated 28 Oct).
3Q26 total revenue reported about $1.2bn, 32% above consensus: advisory +38% vs consensus, ECM +20% vs consensus, institutional equities 4% below consensus.
3Q26 adjusted operating margin reported 22.9%, about 475bps above consensus, from a roughly 425bps non-comp ratio beat and a roughly 50bps comp ratio beat.
3Q26 adjusted comp ratio reported 63.0%, down about 200bps YoY and 50bps QoQ, about 50bps below the Street. GS now forecasts comp leverage of 100bps/60bps/60bps for 2026E/27E/28E.
3Q26 non-comp expenses reported 2% above the Street and up 20% YoY, with a 14.1% non-comp ratio, about 425bps better than the Street.

trade_ideas.description: Buy EVR, 12-month price target $357 (P/E-based, 15.0x on 4Q27E-3Q28E EPS)
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong advisory outlook, expense discipline and estimate upgrades support the stock from here.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker M&A backlogs, longer time to completion pushing out M&A and restructuring revenue, higher compensation pressuring margins, and longer-term share losses.

risk_factors: Weaker M&A backlogs leading to weaker revenue expectations.
Longer time to completion pushing out M&A and restructuring revenue.
Higher compensation expense pressuring pre-tax margins.
Longer-term share losses from slower market or vertical expansion than competitors.
Modestly weaker start to 4Q in ECM.
vol_and_positioning: Investor sentiment on EVR and its peers was strongly negative into the print, which GS cites as a reason for the 13% rally on the day.
